questions.question_text:
One dozen ($12$) tennis balls costs $\$9.60$.
How much do $22$ balls cost?

options.why: Set the equivalent rates up the wrong way round, computing $9.60 \times 12 \div 22$.
Added $\$10$ for the extra $10$ balls, treating the rate as additive instead of multiplicative.
Stopped at the cost of $1$ ball without multiplying by $22$.

questions.question_text:
A computer processes $500$ megabytes in $4$ seconds.
How long does it take to process $3700$ megabytes?

options.why: Divided $3700$ by the $4$ seconds instead of using the $500$ MB per $4$ s rate.
Found how many lots of $500$ MB there are but did not multiply by the $4$ s each lot takes.
Took the reciprocal in the wrong direction, computing $500 \div 3700 \times 4$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{500\text{ MB}}{4\text{ s}} = \dfrac{3700\text{ MB}}{x\text{ s}}$
$\dfrac{4\text{ s}}{500\text{ MB}} = \dfrac{x\text{ s}}{3700\text{ MB}}$
$x = \dfrac{4}{500} \times 3700$
$= 29.6$
It takes $29.6$ seconds.

questions.question_text:
An electric car uses $16$ kWh of electricity per $100$ km.
How far can it travel on a full battery holding $60$ kWh?
Answer to one decimal place.

options.why: Multiplied the $16$ kWh by $60$ instead of scaling the $100$ km distance.
Scaled from $10$ km rather than $100$ km, so the answer is ten times too small.
Assumed each kilowatt-hour covers $100$ km, ignoring that $100$ km uses $16$ kWh.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{16\text{ kWh}}{100\text{ km}} = \dfrac{60\text{ kWh}}{x\text{ km}}$
$\dfrac{100\text{ km}}{16\text{ kWh}} = \dfrac{x\text{ km}}{60\text{ kWh}}$
$x = \dfrac{100}{16} \times 60$
$= 375.0$
It can travel $375.0$ km.

questions.question_text:
The water in a reservoir falls from $430\,000$ litres to $180\,000$ litres over $5$ days.
At the same rate, how many more days will it take to empty completely?

options.why: Found the rate as $430\,000 \div 5$, using the starting volume instead of the volume lost.
Divided the starting volume $430\,000$ L by the rate instead of the $180\,000$ L that remains.
Assumed the rest of the emptying takes the same $5$ days as the first part.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{(430\,000 - 180\,000)\text{ L}}{5\text{ days}} = \dfrac{50\,000\text{ L}}{1\text{ day}}$
$\dfrac{50\,000\text{ L}}{1\text{ day}} = \dfrac{180\,000\text{ L}}{x\text{ days}}$
$\dfrac{1\text{ day}}{50\,000\text{ L}} = \dfrac{x\text{ days}}{180\,000\text{ L}}$
$x = \dfrac{180\,000}{50\,000}$
$= 3.6$
It takes $3.6$ more days.

questions.question_text:
Paint covers $16$ m$^{2}$ per litre.
How much paint is needed for three coats on a rectangular wall $5.2$ m by $2.3$ m?
Answer to two decimal places.

options.why: Painted one coat only, forgetting to multiply the wall area by $3$.
Used two coats instead of the three the question asks for.
Multiplied the area by $16$ instead of dividing by the $16$ m$^{2}$ each litre covers.

questions.solution_text:
Wall area: $5.2 \times 2.3 = 11.96$ m$^{2}$
Three coats: $11.96 \times 3 = 35.88$ m$^{2}$
$\dfrac{16\text{ m}^{2}}{1\text{ L}} = \dfrac{35.88\text{ m}^{2}}{x\text{ L}}$
$x = \dfrac{35.88}{16}$
$= 2.24$
You need $2.24$ L of paint.

questions.question_text:
A camping group uses $24$ litres of drinking water every $5$ days.
They carry $60$ litres.
Will the water last a $13$-day trip?

options.why: Rounded the daily rate of $4.8$ L down to $4$ L before scaling, which understates the water and reverses the decision.
Rounded the $13$ days up to three full $5$-day blocks, overstating the water needed.
Set the equivalent rates up the wrong way round, computing $24 \times 5 \div 13$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{24\text{ L}}{5\text{ days}} = \dfrac{x\text{ L}}{13\text{ days}}$
$x = \dfrac{24}{5} \times 13$
$= 62.4$
No. The trip needs about $62.4$ L but they carry only $60$ L.

questions.question_text:
Fertiliser is spread at $0.2$ kg/m$^{2}$ and sold only in $20$ kg bags.
How many bags must be bought to fertilise $750$ m$^{2}$?

options.why: Left the answer as a decimal, but part bags cannot be bought so it must be rounded up.
Rounded $7.5$ down, which leaves $10$ kg of the area without fertiliser.
Gave the mass of fertiliser in kilograms instead of the number of $20$ kg bags.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{0.2\text{ kg}}{1\text{ m}^{2}} = \dfrac{x\text{ kg}}{750\text{ m}^{2}}$
$x = 0.2 \times 750$
$= 150$
$150 \div 20 = 7.5$ bags
Bags cannot be split, so $8$ bags must be bought.

questions.question_text:
The exchange rate is 179 Japanese Yen = £1.
Which calculation gives the number of pounds in 1000 Japanese Yen?

options.why: Adds the exchange rate instead of converting by division.
Multiplies by the number of yen per pound rather than dividing.
Reverses the required numerator and denominator.

questions.solution_text: Since 179 yen equals £1, convert 1000 yen to pounds by dividing: $1000\div179$.

questions.question_text:
How much is \$6 worth in pounds?
The exchange rates are £1=€1.17 and £1=\$1.31.

options.why: Leaves the dollar amount unchanged instead of converting currencies.
Uses the euro rate rather than the dollar-per-pound rate.
Multiplies by 1.31 instead of dividing to convert dollars into pounds.

questions.solution_text: Since £1=\$1.31, \$6 is $6/1.31=4.58$ pounds to two decimal places.
